subject: Streamed responses dropping & p99 latency spikes (SDK integration retry loop)
messages:
From: Sara Barnes <sara.barnes@checkoutify.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Live checkout streams dropping after SDK upgrade

Hi Stephanie,

We're seeing a severe regression in our live checkout streams since we upgraded to Redwood Node SDK 2.1.4 yesterday evening. Symptoms:
- p99 latency for streamed responses jumps from ~120ms to >1.2s intermittently
- error rate increases (503/stream-termination) causing automatic client retries and duplicated downstream events
- throughput drops under normal load (50 RPS) because many streams are retried and stall

I've attached the last 200 lines of our gateway logs and a short packet capture from a single failing session (error_log_tail.txt, packet_trace.pcap). We haven't changed our integration code other than bumping the SDK.

Can we get someone on a call today? This is impacting a production cohort and our ops team is escalating internally.

Thanks,
Sara Barnes
Head of Infrastructure
Checkoutify

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Live checkout streams dropping after SDK upgrade

Quick triage notes from the first hour (reproduced in our lab against Checkoutify's packet capture):

What we saw
- When the server emits a trailing header block (chunked-ish framing boundary), the Node SDK streaming parser (2.1.4) can misinterpret a split header token across TCP frame boundaries.
- The parser triggers an "early terminal" state instead of buffering the partial header; that results in an abrupt stream termination and the client-side retry logic immediately reopens a new stream.
- The immediate retry loop spikes concurrent requests and causes p99 latency increases and throughput collapse under sustained load.

Evidence (excerpt):
"
[stream-parser] DEBUG parseChunk: saw '\r' then '\n' boundary, header="content-type: application/json\r\nhe"

In the capture attached we observe a header token 'he' split from 'ader' across two TCP frames — the parser currently treats the second frame as a new header set (malformed) and closes the stream.

Workarounds we tested
- Pinning to SDK 2.1.3 fixes the issue
- Introducing a 10ms client-side reassembly buffer avoids the split-token edge case

Attachments: sdk-debug-headers.txt (parser traces + annotated PCAP).

Next steps
- Jonas to open an SDK PR with a defensive reassembly fix; target: hotfix branch + patch release in 24–36 hours.
- Short-term: recommend Checkoutify roll back to 2.1.3 or enable our "streaming_reassembly" compatibility flag (server-side toggle we can flip for your org) until the patch lands.

I'll draft a customer-facing summary for the bridge.

—Sean
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Sara — really sorry for the disruption. Thank you for the packet capture and staying on short notice for the bridge.

Immediate options for Checkoutify:
1) Roll back to Redwood Node SDK 2.1.3 (we verified this removes the failures).
2) We can enable the "streaming_reassembly" compatibility flag on your org immediately (no client change) — this will add ~2–3ms of server-side buffering but prevents the early termination.

We will also:
- Provide a postmortem and a timeline for the SDK patch (targeted 24–36 hours).
- Offer a one-week service credit for impacted production traffic and a follow-up executive call if needed.

Grace will schedule a follow-up after the bridge to confirm the mitigation chosen.

Subject: Re: Streamed responses dropping & p99 latency spikes (SDK integration retry loop)

Sara / Checkoutify team — thank you again for working with us on this. Quick summary and commitments: 

What happened: Our Node SDK 2.1.4 introduced a streaming parser regression that can mis-handle split header tokens across TCP frames, causing premature stream termination and client retry loops.

Actions we are taking (timeline):
- Immediate: We enabled the server-side "streaming_reassembly" compatibility flag for Checkoutify at 16:10 PST on 2026-09-05 (stopgap, no client change).
- Short-term: Hotfix PR #INF-11234 authored by Jonas (reassembly buffer + stricter header-state checks). Target release: 36 hours (roll-forward patch to 2.1.5).
- Alternate: If you prefer rollback, we recommend reverting to SDK 2.1.3; we've prepared rollback instructions and a maintenance window for 02:00–02:30 PST tomorrow to minimize disruption.

Compensation: As a gesture we will apply a one-week service credit for impacted traffic. Grace will send the official CS note.

I'll run point on the executive briefing and postmortem; Sean and Jonas will lead the technical patch. Next touch: scheduled bridge Monday 08:30 PST to confirm patch validation.

Please reply if you'd like us to proceed with the rollback window or to wait for the patch.

—Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
